title: Sports TV Schedule Could Be Tackled For Loss In Aftermath Of FAA’s Nationwide Flight Halt
full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade ‘Sesame Street’ And Cricket Media To Launch Free Streaming Channel Dedicated To The Series Microsoft “Continuing To See Improvements” As Outlook Email, Other Services “Approaching Normal” Microsoft Outlook Still Down In 365 Outage: Company Sees Sporadic Improvements, Though No Sustained Recovery View All November 13, 2026 6:23pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source No. 14 USC made its flight ahead of its game Saturday at No. 5 Indiana Luke Hales/Getty Images College football’s Saturday TV slate appears likely to take a hit from the FAA ‘s decision Friday to impose a ground halt on all U.S. airline traffic, which in turn could disrupt many network sports schedules on a busy weekend. The agency late Friday began allowing flights to depart after more than four hours in a stoppage that saw more than 800 flights diverted and more than 10,000 overall impacted by the first such incident since 9/11. The FAA and the Department of Transportation blamed a “communication issue” that forced the shutdown “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.” Related Stories News FAA Ground Stoppage Could Impact One Of Hollywood’s Busiest Weekends News Nationwide FAA Ground Stop Lifted; Radar “Instability,” Old System Was Root Of Airspace Shutdown, Transportation Secretary Insists In the world of college football, ABC, CBS, NBC, ESPN, Fox and The CW are among networks facing possible game postponements. Media outlets spent the day determining whether teams had either already made it to their game sites, were in the air at the time of the stoppage or had not left their home airports before the shutdown. Watch on Deadline Some schools quickly took alternate means of transportation, with the University of Alabama driving to Nashville for its game against Vanderbilt, while Purdue is taking a bus to Iowa State as is Auburn to Mississippi State, according to the Associated Press. USC arrived ahead of the ban for its game at Indiana, while Boston College made it to South Bend, IN for its game with Notre Dame. The University of Texas, due to travel to play LSU in one of the day’s marquee games, were among several teams forced to deplane before takeoff, like the University of Washington before their trip to Michigan State. Statement from the Southeastern Conference on FAA nationwide ground stop: pic.twitter.com/IIU4TnwMVJ — Southeastern Conference (@SEC) November 13, 2026 Two Friday night games involving ranked teams will have complications for the visitors returning home, with Illinois at UCLA and Houston at Colorado. The NBA is also likely to see some shifting of games, but its Saturday slate is fairly low-wattage compared with Friday night’s Prime Video doubleheader. One story that percolated today: the Brooklyn Nets got stuck on the tarmac in New Orleans trying to get to Memphis to play the Grizzlies on Saturday. The top draw in TV sports, the NFL, seems to have caught a break with the schedule. New England and Detroit are set to play in Germany on Sunday morning, but teams typically travel well in advance of international games in order to adjust to the time difference, meaning they were onsite when the FAA order was given. Depending on the length of the shutdown, there could be a question about the return flights to the U.S. Across the rest of the NFL’s Sunday slate, most games are due to be played by teams within 500 miles of each other, meaning a Saturday bus trip wouldn’t be out of the question. Exceptions include the San Francisco 49ers playing at the Dallas Cowboys; the Seattle Seahawks at the Las Vegas Raiders; and the Miami Dolphins at the Indianapolis Colts. title: 5 Takeaways From China’s Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival
full_text: × Skip to main content By Mathew Scott Plus Icon Mathew Scott View All November 13, 2026 6:19pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Dear You' won both a Special Jury Prize and Best Screenplay at the Golden Rooster Awards. Damai Entertainment China celebrated its Golden Rooster Awards this past Tuesday night in a glittering ceremony hosted inside the palatial Xiamen Strait Grand Theater in Xiamen, Fujian Province, China. The southern seaside city hosted generations of stars — from current hotshot Jackson Yee ( Resurrection ) to acclaimed auteur Zhang Yimou — for an event that is the highlight of the annual state-run Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival. Hong Kong’s Tony Leung Ka Fai stole the show, winning his first Golden Rooster best actor nod for his turn as the villain in the Larry Yang-directed thriller The Shadow’s Edge — some 25 years on from sending hearts a flutter across the globe in Jean-Jacques Annaud’s steamy The Lover . Related Stories Movies 'Fatherland,' 'La Bola Negra,' 'Fjord' Lead European Film Award Nominations Movies Modern Fairy Tale 'Mo Amor' Explores Identity, Transformation and Love in All Its Forms “I hope this is just the beginning of new journey,” said the veteran of more than 140 movies. Behind the scenes the business of making movies was very much front and center, as the Chinese industry gathered for seminars and workshops it hopes will chart its future course. Here’s what The Hollywood Reporter learned from the week: Yimou Urges Filmmakers to Stay Focused on the Story Zhang Yimou brought a sense of gravitas to proceedings across the week. The 76-year-old was there among all the fanfare at the event’s Golden Rooster Awards, handing out the Best Feature Film award to director Shen Ao and his WW2 drama Dead to Rights while also mingling with all the stars and watching on — in awe, like everyone in the room — as a massive dragon drone cruised the air overhead. Yimou had also helped launch the industry side of proceedings with a “Stories That Travel: Chinese and Asian Cinema in Dialogue with the World” seminar that gathered reps from international festivals and, soon enough, saw talk turn to Artificial Intelligence and its effect on cinema. With Zhang’s adaptation of Liu Cixin sci-fi classic The Three-Body Problem in the works the director revealed he’d started to dabble in the tech, with a dedicated team set up on set to explore how AI could be adapted to the filmmaking process. In his own inimitable way, the director then set the scene for the week ahead when he urged his fellow filmmakers to do the same — but to never lose site of the main ingredient: The story. “The new technology is moving too fast,” the director said. “The moment you blink, you are behind it. So, embrace this era. But for me filmmaking is about the story that’s in my heart, and the only thing I can do is to tell it the best way I can.” Star-Studded Golden Roosters Celebrate a Big Year for the Locals The news coming into the week was that so far this year Chinese cinemas have been dominated by Chinese movies, with eight of the year’s box office top 10 being domestic productions. The industry itself has been big on spreading a message of diversification of content, and to that end the two films that dominated “China’s Oscars” could not possibly be more different in either style nor in content. Shen’s Dead to Rights — with Golden Rooster Best Actress winner Gao Ye shining — collected more than $380 million and sets itself around the infamous Nanjing massacre and the real-life story of the photo studio that documented the horror. It’s a gripping often brutal tale — and features two of China’s most bankable stars in Gao and Liu Haoran ( Detective Chinatown ). Lan Hongchun’s Dear You — winner of both Special Jury Prize and Best Screenplay — collected around $300 million and sets itself around the story of one of the thousands of migrant Chinese families separated through economic necessity in the 1950s and ’60s. It’s a languid tear-jerker, and it stars a cast of complete unknowns. Dear You was the surprise hit of the year in China and it reached an enthusiastic global audience. Lan was beside himself on stage. “It feels like I’m dreaming,” he said. “I want to thank my grandma in heaven, because she told me so many stories when I was little.” How Chinese Stories Are Going Global Opening night under the stars at the Bailuzhou Park Water Square in Xiamen was a treat for the young families who packed the venue for the China debut of another film that speaks to the Chinese diaspora and — the filmmakers hope — will to the domestic audience too. The Singapore-Spain-Italy production The Violinist has already won best film at the 2026 Annecy International Animation Film Festival and best animated film at the 19th Asia Pacific Screen Awards. Set among the Chinese community, it follows the fortunes of two childhood friends separated by war, and it had the audience, including all those kids, transfixed. “Singapore’s animation industry is very small, and the country is small too. So, with a production of this scale, one person can’t do it alone,” co-director Ervin Han explained. “We started by looking overseas for co-producers. As it happened, we had a lot of friends in the animation industry. So, all together, we’re telling a story about a part of the history of us Singaporean Chinese.” Producer Cristiano Bortone also took to the stage before the premiere and picked up on what was one of the central themes of this year’s festival: sharing Chinese stories with the world. Bortone The Violinist “delves deeply into Chinese and Asian culture, while also capturing a European style and sensibility.” “This is the beauty of blending our cultures,” he added. AI Creator Opens Up on New Tech China’s next generation was out in force across the industry events, and they basically filled the room at the “Golden Rooster Film Academy II: Ark Lab AI” workshop. Lan Tian, the creative director behind joint-generation AI model Seedance 2.5, took the room and didn’t shy away from exploring its impact in what turned into a candid discussion about how the technology was already impacting the film industry. The AI industry has been embraced in China arguably like anywhere else, and already has an estimated worth of around $176 billion, while the short-drama and digital film market is expected to top $6 billion this year. The pitch from Lan was on the savings the new tech can provide. “If you get an investment of one million, or less than one million you might be able to produce something that looks like it cost 10 million,” he said. But Lan’s push was also to use his technology as a tool that supports “reality.” “My girlfriend is an actor so I know there is concern,” he said. “The creative approach I’m talking about may only require a studio and some props that interact with the actors. But I want this prop to be real, too. For instance, if I need to drink water, I want the water to be real.” Festival Spotlight Turns to Young Filmmakers While AI dominated proceedings, it was encouraging to see young filmmakers committed to the traditions of cinema out and about. Yan Siyu was among those featured during pitching sessions that placed emerging talent in front of international festival and studio reps. Her debut Outside The Room of My Own focusses on the journey three generation of women who take back to their ancestral village, and she echoed the words of Zhang that had opened the whole week. “I want to reach out to people to let them know there is this film in China. It’s a female director’s debut and I can say it’s a really good film,” she said. “This film is not just my work, because I have a lot of people supporting me. I can’t let them down. It’s a story that comes from my heart — and in telling it I am sharing my deepest feelings.” THR

title: Nationwide FAA Ground Stop Lifted; Radar “Instability,” Old System Was Root Of Airspace Shutdown, Transportation Secretary Insists
full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Nationwide FAA Ground Stop Lifted; Radar “Instability,” Old System Was Root Of Airspace Shutdown, Transportation Secretary Insists Microsoft “Deeply Sorry” About Global Outlook Outage, Insists Disruption Caused By “Network Capacity Upgrade” Skydance Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz Spotlights “Moral Responsibility” And Combating Antisemitism & Injustice In Simon Wiesenthal Gala Speech View All November 13, 2026 5:48pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source A view from San Francisco International Airport as the FAA issued a rare nationwide ground stop Getty At 5:15 p.m. PT, the Federal Aviation Administration “lifted” today’s nationwide grounding of thousands of flights. According to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, the root cause of the crisis was a radar “instability” issue that led to the shutting down of domestic airspace Friday at 12:54 p.m. PT. The ground stop lasted almost five hours, with little information from officials and rumors running amok as to what happened and was it nefarious. Related Stories News FAA Ground Stoppage Could Impact One Of Hollywood’s Busiest Weekends Sports Sports TV Schedule Could Be Tackled For Loss In Aftermath Of FAA’s Nationwide Flight Halt Since the FAA issued a rare grounding this Friday the 13th, more than 3,500 flights were taken out of the air. It is estimated that 1.5 million passengers are stranded at airports across the country — from LAX to JFK and everywhere in between. With information being so tight from the feds before Friday night’s White House briefing, a “software update” has been floated as one possible explanation as has an AI system uploading. Now with the radar issues put in focus, on a practical level, the 22 FAA-run Air Route Traffic Control Centers appear to have communication problems. The spillover into the overall system seemed to be unknown, which is why a full-scale shutdown was ordered. Watch on Deadline In great part, the antiquated system was overwhelmed, Duffy said at a ramshackle White House briefing after the ground stop ceased. “It was the old hardware that went down” as routers overloaded, the Real World: Boston alum added of the system heavy1980s and 1990s tech. “None of the new systems went down,” Duffy made a point of noting. All cable news networks went live with the briefing following continuous coverage of the ground stop, which was widely viewed online too. “It is going to continue to fail,” Duffy asserted of the current system. Last year, the GOP-run Congress allocated more than $12 billion to upgrade the admittedly aging air traffic system in Donald Trump ‘s One Big Beautiful Bill. However, as Duffy turned the White House briefing into a partisan praise-a-thon of “builder” Trump and a demand for $50 billion more to upgrade the air traffic system, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin would not rule out today’s disruption was a cyberattack or AI attack. “We are still looking, and we’re not going to rule it out,” the former Oklahoma senator declared. “We have seen zero evidence that this was a cyberattack or SI — Trump’s “super intelligence” phrase — attack,” he added when pressed by reporters. Certainly questions of AI and cyberattacks were poised in the context of Microsoft’s widespread Outlook outage on November 12. That disruption also came following another shock to the digital world with Jensen Huang exiting as CEO of chipmaker Nvidia. Huang was forced to resign from the $4 trillion market capitalized company he founded after admitting to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and amid reports of inappropriate relationships with female Nvidia executives.

title: New Regency Sues Michael Mann to Retain Rights to ‘Heat’
full_text: Skip to main content By Winston Cho Plus Icon Winston Cho View All November 13, 2026 5:35pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Al Pacino and Robert De Niro in 'Heat' (1995). Warner Brothers/Courtesy Everett Collection Logo text New Regency is suing Michael Mann to reassert its ownership over Heat ahead of the high-profile follow-up to the 1995 crime drama classic. In a lawsuit filed Friday in California federal court, New Regency argues that Mann can’t exploit a copyright law provision that allows creators to claw back ownership of their works after a certain period. It seeks a court order clarifying that it retains the rights to the screenplay for Heat . “The Screenplay is not subject to termination,” the complaint states. In a statement, a spokesperson for Mann said the director is “confident that the courts will vindicate Michael Mann’s statutory rights under the Copyright Act.” “This filing has to do with original and personal writing Michael Mann did on multiple screenplays during the 1980s and which evolved into the iconic 1995 film Heat that Mann wrote, produced and directed,” the spokesperson added. “After 40 years, Michael Mann is exercising the right of authors to reclaim their work and, in this case, Michael Mann’s original creation.” The filing comes ahead of Mann preparing to film Heat 2 , a sequel starring Al Pacino, Robert De Niro and the late Val Kilmer. The upcoming film is based on Mann’s 2022 novel of the same name, which serves as both a prequel and sequel to the original. In Friday’s lawsuit, New Regency argues that Mann’s bids to terminate New Regency’s copyright for Heat are invalid because the director penned the screenplay as a work made for hire. Earlier this year, Mann served three notices to New Regency seeking to reclaim the copyright to the screenplay and underlying materials for Heat , setting off a dispute with the company over who owns the rights to the film, according to the complaint. The first notice sought to terminate all copyright grants for Heat , the lawsuit says, including an alleged 1988 oral agreement from Mann and two companies he controlled. The director allegedly later told New Regency that the assignment had never been formally put in writing and that he had only recently discovered the arrangement. The assignment of the copyright is significant because Mann is arguing that he wrote Heat -related materials as an independent author rather than as an employee. The distinction could swing the case since copyrights for works made for hire are generally not eligible to be terminated since the employer, rather than the individual writer, is legally considered the author. “The Termination Notices cloud Regency’s title to the Screenplay and impair its ability to develop, finance, and license works derived from it,” states the complaint. “In addition, certain provisions of the agreements that Mann and Regency each entered into with Amazon with respect to Heat 2 depend on the outcome of this litigation.” Read Mann’s full statement below: This filing has to do with original and personal writing Michael Mann did on multiple screenplays during the 1980s and which evolved into the iconic 1995 film Heat that Mann wrote, produced and directed. After 40 years Michael Mann is exercising the right of authors to reclaim their work and in this case Michael Mann’s original creation. We will vigorously defend this action and are confident that the courts will vindicate Michael Mann’s statutory rights under the Copyright Act. For clarification, this is unrelated to production of Heat 2 which will begin shooting on Jan. 19. THR

title: Trump Says Federal Film Tax Credit Is Gaining Momentum
full_text: × Skip to main content By Winston Cho Plus Icon Winston Cho View All November 13, 2026 4:11pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Donald Trump speaks to reporters before boarding Air Force One at President Donald J. Trump International Airport on November 8, 2026 in West Palm Beach, Florida. Samuel Corum/Getty Images After a sweeping loss at the midterms for Republicans dimmed the short-term prospects of a federal film and TV tax credit, President Trump is pushing for passage of legislation for production subsidies. Trump on Friday said he’s working with lawmakers on both sides of the aisle on the legislation. “The support and popularity of doing this, and bringing Entertainment back to the United States of America, has been unbelievable!” Trump wrote on Truth Social. A bipartisan group of lawmakers has introduced proposed legislation to establish a federal film and TV tax credit, aimed at reshoring production to the U.S. amid a tit-for-tat battle among countries to host Hollywood. If passed, the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act would establish a 20 percent base tax credit on labor expenses, rising to a maximum of 30 percent with bonuses. Only projects with a budget over $1 million, where 75 percent of filming occurs in the U.S., would be eligible for the credit. The subsidy would be stackable on top of individual tax incentives from states, much like the system in several countries that’ve lured production away from the U.S. in recent years. In Friday’s post, Trump said that the entertainment industry has “largely moved to Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and other countries.” “The actors, producers, and all others involved want to come back home!” Trump added. “Importantly, hundreds of thousands of Blue Collar Workers will be positively affected, BIG TIME, by the passage of this Bill.” The post follows Democrats preparing investigations into the Trump administration, raising questions about whether they will focus on film subsidies during the lame-duck session. The tax credit would cost billions of dollars, money that Democrats may be hesitant to attach to a short-term bill during the year-end budget fight. Still, Trump stressed that Democrats are open to the legislation since “much of the money being lost to other countries is coming out of the Blue States.” “The amount of money spent on these Tax Incentives will be made up tenfold by the money pouring into the Treasury’s coffers,” he added. “Meetings are being set up, routinely, with the Leaders of both Parties in order to, GET THIS DONE!” THR

title: How ‘The Basement Yard’ Host Joe Santagato Got Into the World of ‘Hot Ones’
full_text: × Skip to main content By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All November 13, 2026 4:10pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Joe Santagto. Cody Lidtke It’s hard to scroll social media and not come across a clip of Joe Santagato and his podcast The Basement Yard . The creator, a co-host of the podcast alongside Frank Alvarez, is the founder of the online-forward media company Santagato Studios. The podcast is an internet favorite, constantly being clipped and shared online, which has translated into a solid touring business. Now, he’s branching out into something new, if not a bit familiar — the world of Hot Ones . Santagato’s business partner Greg Dybec was approached by First We Feast about a meeting, which they were quick to accept. It all happened a bit fast. “They wanted to start a new show where I would be hosting,” he tells The Hollywood Reporter . Related Stories TV 'Love Trapped' Podcast Coming to TV as Peacock Docuseries News Black Lives Matter Activist DeRay Mckesson Talks Losing Key Trump-Era Protest Mobilization Tool: "I Miss Twitter" “They kind of plucked me and were like, ‘We want to build it around you and we want you guys to be creatively involved as well,'” Santagato says. Enter Hot Ones: Game Night , the Hot Ones spin-off he’s currently hosting and executive producing that finds him interviewing a celebrity guest through a hot sauce-fueled board game. The show’s a perfect fit for the podcaster and creator for many reasons. He’s more than familiar with the world of games, and he’s the co-host of a popular podcast. But Santagato admits he’s still a bit green in one area of the show. “I really don’t have a ton of experience interviewing people,” he says. “I do love talking to people and I definitely gab for a living,” adds Santagato. “But I think I’m kind of approaching it maybe in a different way than someone like Sean Evans would.” *** What’s your approach with Hot Ones: Game Night ? My approach, and what we’ve come to understand, is that this needs to be different [than what Sean Evans does], obviously. They chose me because they wanted [it] to feel more conversational. There’s not a lot of pressure to know everything about this person. We want to see these celebrities in a different sort of light. We’re playing a game, we have the questions. Of course, there is some research that we do. It’s not like we’re going there completely blind. I will and should know things about these people before I’m interviewing them. But for the most part, we’re just two people hanging out is the vibe we’re going for. That’s more fun for them too. They do a lot of interviews with people that maybe a lot of the questions are tweaked slightly and all sound the same and elicit the same sort of response. But if we’re playing a game and we’re trying to make the questions really fun, we can see a little bit more of their personality. My job is to identify those moments and then pull on the string a little further and see how much we can get out of them. It’s supposed to feel like you’re just hanging out with someone or maybe someone you just met and we’ll see how the vibe is. But everyone so far has been great. What’s it like with the guests? You just kind of have to go into it and hope that they’re down to play ball. It’s great because once the initial, I guess, awkwardness of what exactly are we doing sort of dissipates, then it’s a lot of fun. Then people [buy] in and it’s a lot of fun. Also, [now that the show is out] and people can watch it before they come on the show, they’ll have more of an expectation of what it’s going to be. Joe Santagto. Cody Lidtke How is this show different than other interview shows? [We’re] a game and then we’re getting to these questions and maybe having offshoot conversations, but it’s much more loose. It definitely won’t feel, and it doesn’t read as an interview really. You have a lot of agency over the things you’re making at your own company. Do you feel like you’re learning something new working with First We Feast? Definitely. First We Feast, the way that they operate is very professional. They’re super easy to work with, super on top of everything. Nothing is ever late, but nothing feels too pressured to get it done at this exact time or whatever. Their editing and their photos, everything is just great. They operate very well, and it’s not a high pressure environment at all. Everyone seems to be having a good time. Everyone seems to be friends. I truly do enjoy going in there, and I take that back to my studio and the employees that I have and really try to emulate that in that exact same way. It’s nice to know that the thing that I’m trying to accomplish can work on a large scale like what they are doing. You have a background in editing and you know what needs to be happening even though you’re in front of the camera. How are you feeling about everything now? I’m at the point in my career where all these new opportunities are coming in sort of quickly, and this is the biggest one. It’s hard to imagine myself being in the chair and interviewing celebrities, and that’s who I am now. Rather than letting the imposter syndrome prevent me from doing a good job, I’m kind of just doing it scared, for lack of a better word, and showing up. They want me to be me. I’m going to go there and just try to do that and hang out with these people and just see what the hell happens. You do it and then afterwards you can look at that situation and go, “OK, they love it. The edit came out great. I’m watching it. I think it looks good.” I’m definitely more critical than other people will be about it, but I think that is good. Everyone’s going to be like that for themselves. What’s your experience with social media like these days? I feel like I can’t go on social media without seeing videos of you and Frank. Is that your algorithm these days? The luxury that I have from doing this for as long as I have is if I am scrolling on social media, and I can see it’s a clip of me, I just keep going. I don’t need to watch that. It would be weird to indulge in that, but I get it. It helps. I am appreciative of the people who take the time out to cut clips and promote our show in some sort of way. Those people get paid for that, which I’m happy to pay them. I’m not the type of person that will be angry with people who take parts of the show and clip it and make these Instagram accounts or these Instagram or TikTok accounts or even YouTube channels. As long as they’re not posting the entire episode, I don’t care. If you’re making some extra money by clipping the show and your clips are going viral or whatever, I mean, there’s our faces. You’re helping in some sort of way. I do think that was one of the factors as to why the show had a massive growth in the last four years was because of those things. I’m not the type of person to be like, “Hey, just strike that, take that down.” Unless it’s a full episode, then I’m like, “All right, I can’t have this.” But clips, go crazy. THR

title: Ben Stiller Gives Update on His New York Knicks Documentary: “The Pressure Is on”
full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All November 13, 2026 4:08pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ben Stiller at Universal Pictures' 'Focker-in-Law' premiere on Nov. 11, 2026 in New York. Kristina Bumphrey/Variety via Getty Images Ben Stiller is sharing an update on his forthcoming New York Knicks documentary , and after the team’s historic championship earlier this year, he knows “the pressure is on.” While premiering his next film, Focker-in-Law , slated for a Thanksgiving release, on Wednesday night in New York, Stiller teased the documentary to The Hollywood Reporter , describing it as a multi-part project exploring the Knicks’ history. “It’s going to be a multi-part documentary about the history of the Knicks, including this team. It’s about what they’ve meant to New York and hopefully capture the spirit of the team,” he said. Related Stories Movies Elizabeth Holmes' Husband Billy Evans Claims He Didn't Consent to 'You Can See Everything' Nude Shower Scene Movies Margot Robbie to Star in A24's 'The Week of Pain' From 'The Drama' Filmmaker Kristoffer Borgli “It’s been fun to work on so far,” Stiller added, acknowledging the high expectations surrounding the project, especially after the Knicks won their first NBA championship since 1973 on June 13. The documentary was announced shortly afterward , with Stiller directing the project and following the team’s full arc from the ’90s to its record-breaking championship run this year. “I feel like Knicks fans really love the Knicks, so the pressure is on to make something that lives up to what they want, but I hope it does,” Stiller said. As for where the project currently stands, Stiller said it is “in the beginning stages since the playoffs,” adding, “but it’s not gonna be long. We’re full on it.” Stiller, who was born and raised in New York City, has been a lifelong Knicks fan, dating back to his childhood in the early 1970s. He’s also a staple star to sit courtside at games , alongside other celebrity fans including Timothée Chalamet, Spike Lee, Tracy Morgan, Tina Fey and more. When asked if any of those superfans, specifically Chalamet, would appear in the documentary, Stiller said, “Yeah, there definitely are Knicks fans, both known and not known Knicks fans, because I love the community, fans in New York, all over New York, such a huge part of what it means to love the Knicks. So that community is really strong.” Speculation that Stiller is working on a documentary about the NBA team grew after he was spotted filming content during the Knicks’ 2026 Finals run. Immediately after Game 5 of the 2026 NBA Finals , cameras caught up with Stiller, and the Severance executive producer said he was “as happy as I’ve ever felt.” Stiller joked with THR that he would check the score of the Knicks’ Wednesday night game against the Cleveland Cavaliers “right after” finishing interviews at the Focker-in-Law premiere and “periodically” throughout the film’s screening following the red carpet . However, the Knicks lost 115-107. Following the loss, Stiller wrote on X, “What happened.” The Knicks are set to face the Indiana Pacers on Friday night in Indianapolis. THR

full_text: Skip to main content By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter BBC Studios Hires Former Amazon Exec Bree Frank In Production Role ‘Who’s In The Band?’ Music Competition Series From Richard Bacon, Simon Cowell & Savan Kotecha Lands Greenlight At ABC ‘The X Factor’ Reboot In The Works At Fox View All October 13, 2026 12:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source HBO Girls is coming back. HBO has ordered a limited run of five episodes of Lena Dunham ’s hit comedy with the majority of the original cast confirmed to return. Watch the announcement video below. Related Stories News Lena Dunham Has Idea For ‘Girls’ Movie, Jokingly Tries To Force HBO Max’s Hand News Animated Comedy Series ‘Merrick & Treves’ From ‘Archer’ Team Lands Two-Season HBO Order Dunham will reprise her role as Hannah, Allison Williams returns as Marnie, Jemima Kirke is back as Jessa, Zosia Mamet comes back to play Shoshanna, and Andrew Rannells — who recurred as Elijah in the first three seasons before joining the cast as a regular in Season 4 — also is back. There is, however, no sign of Adam Driver, who played Hannah’s boyfriend Adam. Dunham wrote in her recent memoir Famesick that Driver was “verbally aggressive” during filming of the show. Production will begin next year, which will be 15 years after its premiere and 10 years after the Season 6 finale. Watch on Deadline Dunham, who also created Netflix’s Too Much , which premiered last year, long has talked about wanting to return to the Girls universe. Last year, she told Variety that if she had something “really specific” such as millennial women becoming mothers or stepping into menopause, she would “always want to work with those people again.” In that interview, she also suggested Mamet’s Shoshanna was divorced from the New York mayor, Williams’ Marnie is on her third marriage, Jessa is unvaccinated and lives on a boat in Croatia, and Driver’s Adam is a cult theater actor living in Berlin, while Dunham’s own Hannah teaches at Bard and has a son and a chef girlfriend. Dunham created, wrote and directed the series and will exec produce the return alongside Judd Apatow, and Ilene S. Landress and Michael P. Cohen for Good Thing Going. Williams, Kirke, Mamet and Rannells serve as co-executive producers. Jenni Konner, who served as co-showrunner and was a close creative partner to Dunham during Girls , is not returning. In Famesick , Dunham wrote that she hasn’t spoken to Konner since 2018. Dunham said: “We always said we would only return to Girls if there was a specific story we were burning to tell. I’ve missed these characters, but for a long time I couldn’t quite picture them in the present day. Then, right around my 40th birthday, they started talking to me in the shower. And, as you may remember, once this fivesome starts talking, it’s pretty hard to get them to stop. … It’s rare that you get the chance to return to something that changed your life with the gift of hindsight and a whole new level of gratitude and understanding. I love these girls (and boy), our friends at HBO and all the people who have continued to discover the show and remind us afresh why we do this, which is the joy of being together … and the chance to wear yellow mesh…” Amy Gravitt, EVO, Head of HBO & HBO Max Comedy Programming, added: “We’re thrilled to have Lena turn her gaze from the tumult of one’s 20s to the milestone of turning 40. To say the world has changed since we last saw Hannah, Marnie, Shoshanna, Jessa, and Elijah is a massive understatement, but we know fans — old and new — will be happy to see how they’ve grown and relieved to see that they’re still the Girls we knew way back when.” Rare Ground Stop Lifted But Could Affect Busy Hollywood Weekend & Sports Schedule DC Studios To-Do List: What New Boss Will Have From Gunn-Safran Era Johnny Depp Holiday Pic ‘Ebenezer’ Opening To Spirited $20M+ U.S. Sony’s Tom Rothman Launches Major Best Picture Campaign For ‘Brand New Day’ Read More About: 18 Comments

title: James Gunn and Peter Safran’s exit from DC shook the town
full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony DC Studios To-Do List: Here’s What Incoming Boss Jeremy Latcham Will Sort Through From The Gunn-Safran Era Isla Fisher & Blake Ritson Join Al Pacino In John Paul Getty III Kidnapping Pic ‘Captivated’ Johnny Depp Pic ‘Ebenezer’ Opening To Spirited $20M+ U.S. – Box Office Update View All November 9, 2026 9:16am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc James Gunn and Peter-Safran; Jeremy Latcham Getty/John Winters In a seismic executive shuffle unlike anything Bruce Wayne could pull off at Wayne Enterprises, James Gunn and Peter Safran are leaving their posts as co-CEOs and Chairmen of DC Studios , jobs which they’ve held for the past four years. The dynamic duo will continue to produce on various DC projects and are returning to their full-time creative work. They’re currently in post on the Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow which will open in theaters on July 9, 2027. Related Stories Executives Departing DC Co-Head James Gunn Reflects On “Trying” Four Years, Juggling Being Filmmaker & Exec News Skydance Floats First Earnings Report As Hollywood Mega-Studio: Sizing Up The New Empire Taking over the comic book entertainment label as President and Chief Creative Officer is former Marvel SVP of Production and Development, Jeremy Latcham . He starts in the position on Dec. 1 and reports to Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein. Note the tweak here in the reporting structure of DC: Initially the DC Bosses reported straight into the CEO (previously Zaslav, post-merger David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz). Now DC — like the other Warner film labels — reports into Goldberg and Greenstein. Latcham worked with Gunn previously on Guardians of the Galaxy. Latcham shepherded such mega MCU franchises as Iron Man, Guardians of the Galaxy, Spider-Man and The Avengers . He will lead DC’s film, television and animation slate, overseeing the creative pipeline, along with production, talent and strategy. Watch on Deadline
